subject: math

entries: A probability table must add to 1: X = 0, 1, 2 carry probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3, and the chips travel into the sum 0.2 + 0.5 + 0.3 = 1 - something has to happen.
slots.label: A probability table must add to 1
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Expectation: the balance point: E(X) = 0(0.2) + 1(0.5) + 2(0.3) = 1.1, and the fulcrum rises exactly there, where the whole distribution balances.
slots.label: Expectation: the balance point
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Binomial: n = 10, p = 0.3: exactly 3 successes means choosing which 3 of the 10 trials succeed - 120 ways - times one path's probability (0.3)^3(0.7)^7, giving about 0.267.
slots.label: Binomial: choosing the successful trials
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The 68–95–99.7 rule: the shaded band widens from one sigma to three, covering about 68%, then 95%, then 99.7% of the normal curve's area.
slots.label: The 68-95-99.7 rule
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: tails is due after five heads: five heads land one by one, the sixth coin travels in, and the memory needle never moves - the next toss is still 1/2.
slots.label: A common mistake: tails is due
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A list of every value a discrete random variable can take together with its probability: X = 0, 1, 2 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3, and the probabilities always sum to 1.
slots.label: Probability distribution
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The probability-weighted average of a random variable, E(X) = sum of x times P(X = x): for the table above, 0(0.2) + 1(0.5) + 2(0.3) = 1.1, the balance point and long-run mean.
slots.label: Expectation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The count of successes in n independent trials each with success probability p: P(X = r) = (n choose r) p^r (1 - p)^(n - r), as n = 10, p = 0.3 gives P(X = 3) about 0.267.
slots.label: Binomial distribution
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A smooth bell-shaped distribution fixed by its mean and standard deviation, following the 68-95-99.7 rule: about 68% within one standard deviation of the mean, 95% within two, 99.7% within three.
slots.label: Normal distribution
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Events are independent when one outcome does not change another's probability: each coin toss is independent, so after five heads the next toss is still 1/2 heads.
slots.label: Independence
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 probability: distributions, binomial, normal, independence
